title: GRC, Data Privacy & Technical Cybersecurity SME - Senior Manager
description: Cybersecurity: GRC, Data Privacy & Technical Cybersecurity - Senior Manager CFGI is a leading advisory firm that partners with private equity sponsors, portfolio companies, and public companies to solve complex challenges across finance, technology, compliance, and business transformation. Our Cybersecurity practice is rapidly growing and supports clients through cybersecurity governance, risk and compliance (GRC), data privacy, regulatory readiness, technical risk assessments, and operational resilience programs. Role Overview CFGI is seeking a Cybersecurity GRC, Data Privacy & Technical Cybersecurity Subject Matter Expert to lead and deliver strategic advisory engagements that strengthen clients’ security governance, risk management, compliance posture, privacy programs, and technical security capabilities. This role combines hands-on delivery, executive communication, and practice leadership. The successful candidate will translate technical security risks into business impact, assess whether controls are appropriately designed and implemented, and partner with CISOs, CIOs, CFOs, General Counsel/Privacy Counsel, Risk Leaders, technology teams, and PE deal teams to drive pragmatic, measurable outcomes. The ideal candidate brings deep GRC and privacy expertise together with sufficient technical depth to challenge control owners, evaluate cybersecurity architectures and operations, validate evidence, and connect technical findings to regulatory, risk, and business requirements. Key Responsibilities Client Advisory & GRC Delivery Lead end-to-end GRC and privacy engagements, including scoping, planning, execution, quality review, and executive reporting. Design and operationalize cybersecurity governance models, including policies, standards, risk appetite, committees, reporting, KPIs, and KRIs. Build and mature enterprise risk programs, including risk assessments, risk registers, control libraries, control rationalization, and control testing approaches. Develop and implement security policies, standards, and procedures aligned to NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-53, ISO 27001/27002, CIS Controls, SOC 2, CMMC, and FedRAMP. Support regulatory readiness and compliance initiatives, including SEC cyber disclosure support, NYDFS 500, GDPR/UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOX ITGC, CMMC, and FedRAMP alignment where applicable. Stand up or enhance privacy programs, including data mapping and inventories, DPIAs/PIAs, DSAR processes, retention, consent management, third-party privacy risk, and privacy by design. Perform vendor and third-party risk assessments and implement scalable TPRM operating models. Technical Cybersecurity Assessment & Advisory Assess technical security controls across cloud, network, endpoint, identity, application, data, and security operations environments, and connect control gaps to business and regulatory risk. Evaluate security architecture and configuration evidence for common platforms and services, including Microsoft Azure, AWS, Microsoft 365, identity providers, firewalls, EDR/XDR, SIEM, vulnerability management, backup, and data protection technologies. Review identity and access management capabilities, including privileged access, multifactor authentication, joiner-mover-leaver processes, access reviews, service accounts, and segregation of duties. Assess vulnerability and patch management processes, interpret scan results, validate remediation prioritization, and evaluate exposure management practices. Evaluate logging, monitoring, detection, and incident response capabilities, including alert coverage, escalation workflows, playbooks, tabletop exercises, and lessons learned. Assess secure configuration, network segmentation, encryption, key management, backup and recovery, data loss prevention, and resilience controls. Partner with technical teams to validate control implementation through interviews, documentation, configuration samples, screenshots, reports, tickets, and other evidence. The role is not expected to serve as a full-time engineer but must be able to credibly challenge technical assumptions and distinguish documented controls from operating controls. Support cyber due diligence, post-acquisition integration, carve-outs, and rapid maturity uplift by identifying material technical risks and developing prioritized remediation roadmaps. Executive Communication & Stakeholder Management Translate complex technical, regulatory, and privacy requirements into clear, business-oriented recommendations. Deliver executive-ready artifacts, including board and audit committee materials, risk heatmaps, maturity assessments, target operating models, roadmaps, and dashboards. Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leadership; present findings confidently, facilitate difficult risk decisions, and influence action across business and technology stakeholders. We believe doing the right thing for our clients and our associates is good business . With a career at the firm, y ou can expect opportunities to create real impact at work and in your community. Y ou’ll enjoy resources to support your career path, a s well as compensation , benefits , and flexibility to enrich your life. Here, you’ll find a collaborative culture that respect s and valu e s differences and colleagues who share a spirit of generosity . Join us for the opportunity to g row and make a difference in ways that matter to you . Role Summary In this role as Director, Regulatory Advisory Compliance, you will lead a team within T. The role is responsible for execution strategy, risk-based prioritization, and senior stakeholder alignment across distribution and assurance business units. The successful candidate will bring extensive experience supporting SEC-registered investment advisers, broker-dealer trading, and operations with complex, multi-entity financial services organizations. The role spans current and emerging advisory and wealth capabilities and requires the ability to translate regulatory requirements into practical guidance, disclosures, policies, controls, supervision, training, and governance across legal entities, client channels, and third-party relationships. Leads complex cross-functional regulatory initiatives, represents Global Distribution Compliance & Risk Management in governance forums, and supports examinations, audits, compliance testing, and remediation activities. Qualifications Required: Bachelor’s degree or the equivalent combination of education and relevant experience and 10+ years of experience in investment adviser compliance, financial services regulatory compliance, Legal, regulatory risk, regulatory consulting, or a related discipline. title: Manager, Technical Accounting and Equity Reporting
description: Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles. Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office. As Oura scales and prepares for life as a public company, equity compensation and non-routine technical accounting questions are becoming larger and more complex. We’re looking for a Manager, Technical Accounting and Equity Reporting to own stock-based compensation accounting and equity reporting end to end, and to serve as a technical accounting resource on complex and non-recurring transactions.You’ll own ASC 718 accounting and the equity roll-forwards, reconciliations, footnotes, and disclosures that flow from it; work through the accounting for share repurchases; document accounting positions in clear memos; and build SOX-ready processes and controls. You’ll partner closely with Legal, Stock Administration, Payroll, Tax, Corporate Finance, FP&A, Business Systems, and our external auditors. What You Will Do: Stock-based compensation accounting (ASC 718) Own the monthly stock-based compensation close: validate grant, vesting, forfeiture, and termination data, calculate and record expense by function, and prepare the related journal entries. Review valuation inputs and assumptions (e.g., Black-Scholes, 409A) with valuation specialists and support the related audit evidence. Account for modifications, cancellations, repurchases, and settlement mechanics, including net share settlement. Reconcile the cap table and equity administration platform to the general ledger, and resolve differences promptly. Equity reporting and disclosures Prepare and review equity roll-forwards, APIC and stockholders’ equity activity, and stock-based compensation disclosures for quarterly and annual financial statements. Maintain audit-ready support and tie-outs for every equity figure in the financial statements and disclosures. Liquidity events and capital structure Lead the accounting analysis for tender offers, secondary transactions, IPO-related events, and corporate reorganizations as they affect employee equity. Lead the modeling process around the expected financial statement impact of an IPO on equity awards, including expense recognition, net settlement, and tax withholding, and keep the model current as timing and terms evolve. Technical accounting and policy Research complex accounting questions under US GAAP and write clear, well-supported technical memos that document facts, guidance, analysis, and conclusions. Serve as a technical resource on non-routine transactions beyond equity, as needed - areas could include: debt vs. equity accounting (ASC 480), debt (ASC 470), leases (ASC 842), business combinations (ASC 805), and global entity matters. Assist with drafting, updating, and maintaining accounting policies, and monitor new standards and SEC guidance for their impact on Oura. Controls and audit Design, document, and operate key controls over equity and technical accounting in partnership with the SOX team, and remediate gaps promptly. Serve as a primary contact for external auditors on equity and technical accounting, including walkthroughs, PBC requests, and technical discussions. What you'll bring 6+ years of progressive accounting and financial reporting experience, including Big 4 or national firm experience. Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance; active CPA strongly preferred. Hands-on expertise in ASC 718, including options, RSUs, performance-condition awards, modifications, repurchases and tender offers. Strong working knowledge of US GAAP and SEC reporting, with experience in ASC 718. Experience producing equity roll-forwards, footnotes, and disclosures for audited financial statements, and reconciling an equity administration platform (e.g., Carta, Shareworks) to the general ledger. Demonstrated ability to research complex technical matters independently and write defensible accounting memos. Experience designing and operating SOX or other internal controls over financial reporting. Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining complex topics to non-accounting partners, and a record of mentoring or managing others. Nice to have: Public company or IPO-readiness experience. Workiva and Shareworks experience. Experience in consumer hardware, health technology, or subscription businesses. Benefits At Ōura, we care about you and your well-being. Everyone here at Ōura has a ring of their own and we are continually looking to improve employee health. What we offer: Competitive salary and equity packages Health, dental, vision insurance, and mental health resources An Ōura Ring of your own plus employee discounts for friends & family 20 days of paid time off plus 13 paid holidays plus 8 days of flexible wellness time off Paid sick leave and parental leave Ōura takes a market-based approach to pay, which may vary depending on your location. US locations are categorized into tiers based on a cost of labor index for that geographic area. While most offers will be closer to the starting range, successful candidates' pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location, internal peer equity, and market conditions. These ranges may be modified in the future. Region 1 $143,650-$169,000 Region 2 $130,050-$153,000 Region 3 $117,300-$138,000 A recruiter can determine your Region based on your US location. We are not considering candidates residing in the following states: Alaska (AK), Delaware (DE), Iowa (IA), Mississippi (MS), Nebraska (NE), South Dakota (SD), West Virginia (WV), and Wisconsin (WI). title: AI Governance Lead - Finance
description: NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world. We are looking for an AI Governance Lead to join the Finance AI team at NVIDIA. This role will drive just enough process for compliance and security, without losing the innovation that defines our start-up culture. As AI agents and automation spread across Finance, our governance lead will build the intake, risk triage, and approval flow that lets the right tools move quickly and keeps the wrong ones away from financial data. Act as a trusted partner to Finance’s citizen developers, Internal Audit, Security, Legal, and IT while writing the playbook for how a finance org adopts AI without compromising the controls that protect it! What you’ll be doing: Lead the governance path for AI tools and agents across Finance. Set and enforce guardrails for agents that touch financial or regulated data in partnership with data owners, IT, and external vendors. Make it easy to do the right thing by providing clear, consistent, implementable guidance and documentation / documentation-as-code. Reduce process lift by creating reusable pre-approved patterns that developers and analysts can follow. Learn and use the latest AI technology while translating emerging AI-specific risks into practical, applicable decision criteria. What we need to see: A track record of building a governance, controls, or process function from the ground up. Fluency in financial controls and SOX, plus knowledge of the broader regulatory landscape. Familiarity with data classification and third-party/vendor risk. Enough technical literacy in system architecture, Databricks, and AI technologies to ask the right questions, challenge a design, and know when an answer doesn't add up. 8+ years of professional experience across controls, audit, risk, governance, information security, technical program management, or a strong record in a related field. BS/MS in finance, accounting, information systems, or equivalent experience. Ways to stand out from the crowd: Experience governing or auditing AI, automation, or emerging technology in a regulated environment. Experience standing up cross-functional review or approval processes (architecture review boards, change advisory, vendor risk, or third-party AI review). Excellent communication skills, including experience driving decisions through complex environments. An enthusiastic consumer of AI research. You read about exploits and vulnerabilities and catalogue the risks and solutions! Widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers, NVIDIA offers highly competitive salaries and a comprehensive benefits package. As you plan your future, see what we can offer to you and your family www.nvidiabenefits.com/ Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are: 136,000 USD – 212,750 USD for Level 4; and 148,000 USD – 235,750 USD for Level 5. You will also be eligible for equity and benefits .
